defects: [Major] Split-billet ends in the woodpile are visibly faceted octagons (view 1 pile face, view 6 bottom edge), right at eye height beside the wall.
[Major] Open black slot between the lintel log and the head of the side window, with thin pale pins showing through it (view 6, above the frame at right): the frame does not fill the cut opening.
[Major] Roof hole on the porch slope has dead-straight sheet edges over tidy, evenly spaced rafters (views 3, 4, 5): reads as two panels neatly removed, not storm or rot damage.
[Minor] Porch posts butt into the underside of the log plate with no notch, pin or brace (view 4 post under the plate end).
[Minor] Eave rust is the same even strip along every sheet (views 2, 5) with no heavier runs at laps or fixings.
fixes: Raise radial segments on billet ends to 12+ or bake a rounded normal, and vary split faces so ends are not uniform polygons.
Extend the window head board up to the lintel log and add a chinked filler strip so no void remains above the frame.
Tear the hole: bend and curl one sheet edge upward, leave a hanging fragment, snap one rafter and add rot staining around the opening.
Cut a saddle into the plate log at each post head and add a spike or diagonal brace.
Break up the eave rust mask with drips running down from laps and nail lines, heavier at sheet overlaps.

defects: [Major] Close view (panel 6) is fully black: the close-up camera shows nothing, so material quality at touching distance is unverified on this sheet.
[Major] Door is a flat green slab with a single nub handle and no visible hinges, closer or lock (view 4).
[Major] Concrete step is off-centre, starting mid-doorway and running right beneath the window, so it does not serve the door (view 4).
[Major] Straight vertical seam runs from the window sill to the ground through the block courses (view 4, right of the door), and the base damp is a uniform gradient around the whole building.
[Minor] Power cable lies loose on top of the ground for about 9 m and simply stops (views 2, 3, 5); the roof vent is an oversized mushroom on a thin stalk.
fixes: Reframe the close camera on the door and rerender; do not resubmit without a usable close-up.
Model a steel door: three barrel hinges, lever and hasp, frame stop, pressed panel lines, and paint chipped around the handle and lower edge.
Centre the step on the door opening and shorten it to about door width plus 200 mm each side.
Remove the seam by offsetting UVs or making it a real control joint with sealant; replace the damp gradient with streaks under the roof overhang, pipe and box.
End the cable in a junction post or bury it with a conduit riser; shrink the vent to a realistic cowl with a flange.

defects: [Major] Reads as an air compressor rather than a generator: horizontal tank-like body, finned block and no obvious alternator housing, fuel tank or output terminals (views 1, 2, 4).
[Major] Dark gap between the plinth and lower skid with a pale sliver of daylight at its left end (view 2, base front); the machine is not visibly bolted to the skid.
[Major] Radial pinched creases at the pole of the tank end-cap (views 1 and 4) look like a shading fault, and the body carries unexplained thin raised slashes and a cross (views 1, 4, 5).
[Minor] Control box back and sides are blank smooth blocks with no door seam, fixings or vents (views 1, 6).
[Minor] Paint on body and tank is nearly clean while only skid edges and fins rust; no oil, soot at the exhaust or fuel staining.
fixes: Rebuild the cylinder as an alternator: ribbed housing, end bell, terminal box and cooling slots, and add a fuel tank with cap and line above the engine.
Close the plinth-to-skid gap with channel rails and visible anchor bolts at each corner.
Fix end-cap topology to remove the pole pinch; replace the slashes with stencilled data plate and real weld seams.
Give the control box a hinged cover with screws, gland nuts and a conduit entry.
Add soot around the exhaust, oil weep beneath the block and fuel stain below the filler.

defects: [Major] Red paint appears on the cross-braces only while the legs stay white in the same band (view 6): real banding covers whole sections, so this reads as a material-assignment accident.
[Major] Back of the two upper dishes is mottled brown while the others are clean white (view 1), with no cause; dish finishes do not agree.
[Major] Base is bare: legs land directly on a plain slab with no base plates, cable tray, equipment cabinet, fence or grounding (view 6).
[Minor] Guy wires are hairline and vanish against the sky (views 1-4), with only a tiny fitting at each anchor block.
[Minor] No weathering story on the concrete or steel: no rust at bolted splices, no staining under the platform.
fixes: Paint complete tower sections in alternating red and white, legs and braces together, with chalked fade.
Use one dish back material with rust concentrated at the feed mount and rim bolts.
Add base plates and anchor bolts, a cable ladder down one leg into an equipment cabinet, and a chain-link pen.
Thicken guys to about 16 mm cable with thimbles, turnbuckles and rust at the anchor eyes.
Add rust bleed at splice plates and rain staining streaks under the platform and on the slab.

defects: [Major] Wear is too even: timber is one uniform grey top to bottom with no rot at the footings, missing boards or staining beneath the cab (views 1, 6).
[Major] Cab roof from above is a pale, almost clean pyramid with faint ribs (view 5), far less convincing than the structure beneath it.
[Minor] Concrete piers are plain boxes with bare steel shoes and no spalling or splash staining (view 6).
[Minor] Bracing is uniformly intact at every bay; nothing has failed on a tower that is meant to look abandoned (views 1-4).
fixes: Darken and rot the lowest metre of each leg, add water staining beneath joints and landing edges, and remove or crack several tread and deck boards.
Replace the roof with lapped sheets, rusted ridge cap and fasteners, and add moss in the lower corners.
Chip pier edges, add splash-back soil staining and rust trails from the shoes.
Snap one diagonal, leave a hanging brace and repair one bay with a mismatched timber.

defects: [Major] Ragged black gap between the back of the plank hood and the rock face (view 5, above the portal; view 1 upper left of the set): the timber set does not meet the hillside.
[Major] Danger sign title is a pale smeared block and the red line beneath is garbled (views 2, 6): the only text at the portal is unreadable.
[Major] Spoil pieces are rock-textured cuboids spread almost symmetrically either side of the track with logs in matching clusters (views 5, 6): reads as placed primitives.
[Major] Ore cart is a clean trapezoid box with one dead-straight rust band and a faceted low-poly dome of ore (view 6).
[Minor] Portal posts are plain cylinders landing on small blocks with no sill, wedges or cap pieces at the lintel joints (view 6).
fixes: Extend the hood planks into the rock and pack the junction with rubble, dirt and a timber lagging board so no void shows.
Rework the sign at higher resolution with a legible DANGER heading and hand-stencilled text, then age it.
Replace cuboids with irregular broken rock meshes, group them into one spoil heap downhill of the portal, and let timber lie where it would have fallen.
Add riveted plate seams, dented rim and rust that follows seams and the floor; replace the ore dome with a heap of individual rock pieces.
Add a mud sill, wedges and cap blocks at each post, and square the post tops into the lintel.

defects: [Major] Tarp mound is a smooth, clay-brown lump with no folds, tension lines or hint of what lies under it, and reads as mud or dough (views 1, 5, 6).
[Major] Tarp hold-down stones are near-identical small cubes set in an even row along one edge (views 1, 5).
[Major] Tent canvas is cloudy green mottling on flat planes, with no seam lines, ridge sag or stain logic (views 1, 3).
[Major] Bedroll reads as a smooth pale gas cylinder with straps (views 3, 6), and the props are spaced like a catalogue with no signs of a hurried departure.
[Minor] Log seat end grain is faceted and the laundry posts are oversized for a single small cloth (views 1, 4, 6).
fixes: Resculpt the tarp over a recognisable form with folds and tension from the stones; add a dark wet line and a corner lifted to hint at the contents.
Use varied natural rocks at uneven spacing, only where the wind would have lifted the tarp.
Add stitched seams, reinforced corners, sag between guy points and damp staining rising from the ground.
Rebuild the bedroll as compressed cloth with creases and tie marks; restage props in a disturbed layout with an overturned pot and scattered items.
Smooth the log ends and swap the line posts for slim poles or a rope between trees.

defects: [Major] Logs are straight, same-diameter cylinders with no taper, knots, limb stubs or crook (views 1, 2, 5), so the stacks read as pipes in bark texture.
[Major] End grain is uniform pale tan on every log with little ring or saw detail and no staining (views 2, 4).
[Major] Shed rear wall is one large flat plane of striped plank texture with no battens, fixings or gaps (view 3).
[Major] Stack stakes are lone thin posts that restrain nothing visibly: no chains, wedges or bunks under the bottom layer (views 1, 2, 6).
[Minor] Cable reel is a blank grey spool with plain faces and no cable (views 1, 2, 5).
fixes: Vary radius, taper and bend per log and add sawn limb stubs and bark-loss patches.
Give ends ring and chainsaw-mark variety, tree numbers in paint and grey weathering on older logs.
Model individual boards with battens, nails, a few gaps and one loose board.
Add bunks under each stack and wedge or chain the stakes so they visibly hold the load.
Wrap the reel with partly unwound cable, add a stencil and flange rust.

defects: [Major] Black rectangular corners show above the pointed window arches (views 1, 2, 3): the wall opening is square while the trim is arched.
[Major] Clapboard texture is smeared horizontally and low resolution at close range (view 6, either side of the window).
[Major] Dark grime along the base forms hard-edged, patchy shapes stamped on the wall and reads camouflage-like (view 1, front and corner; view 4 door side).
[Minor] Eave rust is a similar band along the whole roof with bright, clean roof planes above it (views 2, 3).
[Minor] Graveyard fence stops as a series of straight runs with little sag, breakage or leaning posts (views 2, 3).
fixes: Cut gothic-pointed wall openings to match the trim, or fill the corners above the arch with spandrel boards.
Re-unwrap siding at proper texel density and author paint peel at 2K so it stays sharp at 1 m.
Replace the grime patches with a soft capillary damp gradient, soil splash at the base and growth concentrated at downpipes and corners.
Vary roof rust by sheet, add streaks from fasteners and darken planes where the tower shadows them.
Lean a few fence sections, drop one panel, rust the post bases and let weeds interrupt the run.

defects: [Major] Rear face shows the same pale flecks repeating plank after plank (views 1, 2), an obvious stamp pattern on a surface you will walk past.
[Major] Wear is uniform; posts run straight into the ground with no rot, cracks or splash staining at the base (views 1-4, 6).
[Minor] Bright white streak along the roof ridge blows out in view 2, top right.
[Minor] Missing person photo is only a brown blur and the board lacks pinned scraps, staple remnants or torn paper layers (view 4).
[Minor] Thin slits of sky show between roof boards with no sign of missing or lifted boards to explain them (views 1, 2).
fixes: Offset UVs per board and vary stains so no two adjacent planks share marks.
Add rot, soil line and dark wicking at the post bases, and notch the rails into the posts with visible bolts.
Reduce the ridge cap specular and give it a matte weathered metal or wood material.
Replace the blur with a degraded but readable face photo and add torn poster layers and rusty staples.
Either close the slits with battens or make them deliberate with a lifted or absent board.

defects: [Major] X-braces and rails pass through each other and into the legs with no notch, bolt or nailed plate at most joints (view 6 crossing and leg ends).
[Major] Identical neat green lashing at every leg and level (views 1-6) looks brand new and machine-repeated.
[Minor] Corrugated roof is a single clean sheet resting on post tops with little visible fixing (views 1-3, 5).
[Minor] Wear stops at the texture: no broken rung, split brace or rot at leg feet (views 1-4).
fixes: Add half-lap notches, carriage bolts or gusset plates at crossings and leg joints.
Replace with varied wire ties, rope and bolts; fray one, and leave a rust stain where wire has bitten in.
Add a ridge sag, nails with rust halos and roof purlins fixed to the posts.
Split a brace, crack one ladder rung and add rot and soil marks at the feet.

defects: [Major] Transformer reads as a plain dark capsule against the pole with no visible hanger bracket, cooling fins, bushings or nameplate (views 1-5).
[Major] Base is unweathered where it enters the ground: no creosote wicking, ground-line rot or checks (view 6).
[Minor] Crossarm hardware is sparse: braces and insulators read correctly but carry no rust, bolts or tie wires (views 3-5).
[Minor] Step bolts are tiny dark ticks that barely read (views 1, 2, 6).
fixes: Model the can with a lid and clamp ring, cooling ribs, primary and secondary bushings and two hanger irons bolted through the pole.
Darken and rot the lowest 400 mm, add ground-line check cracks and a tag plate.
Add through-bolts, washers, rust streaks and tie wire around the insulators.
Increase step size to realistic 16 mm bolts with bent ends.

defects: [Major] Pale edge-wear halo traces the outline of the lid in a continuous band (views 1-5), reading as a mask rather than wear.
[Major] The same pale scar mark repeats on multiple boards and faces (views 1, 4, 6).
[Minor] Rust hasp is a flat strip on one side with no pin, staple or matching lock point (views 3, 4).
[Minor] Corner posts stop short of the lid corners, leaving a stepped notch unresolved at each corner (views 1-3).
fixes: Make edge wear break up per board, heavier on corners and handling points, with some clean edges.
Vary board UV offsets and rotate or replace the repeated scar on each face.
Model a hasp with hinge pin, staple and padlock or torn fixing.
Run corner posts to the lid underside and add a metal corner cap or nailed edge strip.

defects: [Major] Automatic floating gate fails and the images back it: the lid and bungs float as a separate disc with a dark gap all round inside the rim (views 1, 3, 4, 6), not rolled into the chime.
[Major] DIESEL stencil is mirrored and sits on a visibly darker rectangle cut by the hoop (views 1, 4, 6).
[Major] Lid colour is a washed-out pink against a dark red body (view 2), and the hollow dish bungs look like small cups rather than threaded caps.
[Major] Rust is confined to the lower third and stops abruptly at the hoop line (views 1, 4, 6); upper body is a nearly clean flat red with faint vertical faceting.
[Minor] No dents or bottom-chime damage beyond one hoop wobble (view 2).
fixes: Weld the lid into the rim: rolled double seam, slight recess and no gap, with bungs flush and joined.
Flip the decal UVs and stencil directly into the paint, broken by the hoop and chipped.
Match lid and body paint with sun fade, and rebuild the bungs as threaded plugs with a recessed slot.
Add rust at the chime and hoops, drips down the seam and paint chipping; let the rust edge fade gradually.
Add impact dents, a crushed chime section and a dark residue trail below a bung.

defects: [Major] Side faces read as cloth sheets draped on the body: edges curl away at corners (views 1, 3, 4) with a dark standing gap on the left flank (crop of view 1).
[Major] X pressing is soft fabric-like shading on the sheet instead of a stamped steel recess (views 3, 4).
[Major] Rust rod along each side seam looks like a stuck-on stick rather than a welded seam (views 1, 2, 5).
[Major] Body is a chamfered prism with a separate flat top plate, with no rolled seam joining shell and top (views 1-3).
[Minor] Bottom rust is a single blotchy band without scratches or seam corrosion (views 2, 3).
fixes: Rebuild the body as a single shell with the X pressed in as real geometry, so no sheet sits proud of the body.
Model the raised X with a crisp normal bake and paint scuffs along its ridges.
Replace the rod with a continuous rolled weld seam around the shell, rusted along the crown.
Add a rolled top seam, recess the cap mount and connect the handles to a single base bar.
Build rust from edges and seams, with scratches through the paint at carrying points.

defects: [Major] Bright white crescent shows at one cap where the barrel does not sit concentric in the brass (views 2, 3, 4), looking like exposed filler.
[Minor] Barrel is clean aside from light mottling, with no heat browning, scorch or tarnish on the caps (view 6).
[Minor] Brass reads as an even mustard tint without burnish at the bolt holes or edges (views 1, 6).
fixes: Centre the barrel in the caps and replace the white ring with a thin ceramic step and solder fillet.
Add heat discolouration near one end, label wear and hairline crazing.
Burnish tab contact areas and hole edges, and add verdigris in crevices.

defects: [Major] Base is an open black bowl around the post with bare ground inside (views 1-3, 5, close-up crop): no concrete, no fixing, reads as a dog dish.
[Major] Yellow face is sponge-mottled in camouflage-like blotches (views 3, 4).
[Major] Post is a plain smooth pipe with no cap detail, rust or banding, and straps barely read at the sign (views 1, 2, 6).
[Minor] Back panel carries a fine grid-like pattern at a distance (views 1, 2, 5).
[Minor] Only damage is a few dark holes; no impact bend, sticker residue or rust trails from bolts (views 3, 4).
fixes: Replace the bowl with a broken concrete collar and soil mound, or drive the post straight into the ground with a kink.
Replace blotches with sun fade, peeling reflective film and rust bleeding from the bolt holes.
Add a rounded post cap, rust at bolt positions and a slight lean or bend.
Use a clean galvanised back material with cross bracing and weathering runs.
Add a bullet hole cluster with rust trails, a bent corner and old sticker remains.

defects: [Major] Tread is one row of long jagged spikes that looks like a saw blade or crown, not lugs (all views), far too sharp for rubber.
[Major] Tread splits along a centre line with torn, jagged triangles (views 3, 6), reading as two tyres fused or a broken mesh.
[Major] Sidewall is featureless: no bead, lettering, moulded ribs or wheel seat (views 1-5).
[Major] Lugs melt together in smeared brown shading with no dirt logic (views 1, 4, 6).
[Minor] 4800 triangles is expensive for a scattered tyre if it counts as background; if so the 2.5k gate also fails.
fixes: Remodel the tread as blocky chevron or road lugs with flat tops and rounded shoulders.
Close the centre seam and make the carcass continuous, with one deliberate cut or tear.
Add a bead ring, moulded sidewall lettering and fine rib detail by normal map.
Bake clean rubber with dirt packed in the grooves, sun cracking and mud at the lower arc.
Reduce to 2.5k with a bake, or confirm the budget class.

defects: [Major] Satellite stones are fused to the main mass by narrow necks and read as stubby limbs (views 2, 3, 5), most obviously the dog-bone lobe in view 3.
[Major] Moss and lichen are spread evenly on every face regardless of orientation (views 1-4), so the texture reads as an all-over mottled wrap.
[Major] Close view is soft and blurry (panel 6), with no sharp grain or fracture at 1.7 m.
[Minor] Tiny white specks at facet edges (view 2), and a dark undercut at the base without any ground contact logic (view 3).
fixes: Separate the satellites into independent stones partly buried at the base, and delete the necks.
Mask moss to upward faces and crevices, leave drier rock on steep faces, and add a water line.
Add a detail normal and tiling albedo at about 1 m scale to sharpen close range.
Fix open or sliver vertices and fill undercuts with soil or broken talus.

defects: [Major] Boulder lobe at the base is a rectangular peninsula on a stalk (views 1, 2, 5), unnatural and unconvincing.
[Major] Main mass is a chopped, flat-sided block with straight facet shadow lines (views 1, 3).
[Major] Lichen coverage matches rock_a almost exactly, even on shaded faces (views 1-4), and the close view is soft (panel 6).
[Minor] No fracture debris or soil at the contact; base simply ends on a clean skirt (views 2, 4).
fixes: Delete the stalk and place a separate partly buried stone instead.
Break up planar faces with secondary fractures and displacement, and soften some facet lines.
Use a distinct moss mask and hue variant from rock_a, driven by orientation and crevices.
Add broken talus and leaf litter contact to the skirt.

defects: [Major] Horizontal ledge on the lower front shows smeared, stretched texture along the fold (view 4).
[Major] Dark vertical bands with straight edges on the fractured side look painted on (view 3).
[Minor] Close view is soft (panel 6), with white specks along upper edges in views 2 and 5.
[Minor] Moss is evenly applied rather than collecting in the cracks and ledges (views 1-4).
fixes: Reproject UVs on the ledge or add a triplanar blend there.
Replace the painted bands with geometry: real recessed fractures with occlusion.
Add a sharper detail layer and clean degenerate sliver triangles.
Concentrate moss in cracks and ledge tops and dry the steep faces.

defects: [Major] Reads as a bevelled wedge or truncated pyramid with a single sharp vertical corner (views 1, 2, 3), and almost no secondary fracture or overhang.
[Major] Uniform lichen wrap with no orientation logic (views 1, 2, 4), and flat dark sides that look like a single material.
[Major] Close view is smeared and soft (panel 6), losing the rock grain at walking distance.
[Minor] Isolated pit on the upper face looks like a dent stamped into an otherwise smooth surface (view 3).
fixes: Break up the wedge with stepped cleavage planes, an undercut and a split block.
Mask moss to top surfaces and fissures, and add dry grey facing on the weather side.
Add a high-frequency detail normal and sharpen the albedo.
Replace the dent with a fissure continuing around the form.
